newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer amid overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer amid overseas buying.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger on Monday, extending gains made on Friday, as a firmer currency and overseas buying helped boost prices, dealers said.

"It's just a continuation of the strength we have been seeing," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "We're seeing overseas buyers of longer bills, one-year bills, overnight from the Far East. And the currency is doing a little bit better."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 2.84 percent from 2.85 percent at Friday's close.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets made strong gains on Friday following a U.S. report showing an unexpected fall in the producer price index for May. The report reduced expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will hike rates in July.

Canada's dollar, which also gained on Friday, opened stronger at C$1.3769 (US$0.7262) on Monday as inflation fears subsided and investors continued to buy Canadian assets on overseas markets, traders said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.10 percent from 3.13 percent. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.57 percent from 3.62 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.0 percent, the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
